issues.legal_issue: Pending civil litigation over the same property does not by itself justify quashing criminal proceedings where the first information report contains specific, serious allegations that prima facie disclose criminal offences and are not frivolous or mala fide.
material_facts: The first information report alleged that the appellant fraudulently procured a power of attorney by forging the signatures of the persons said to have executed it, and then sold the land under that authority.
The report alleged that one purported signatory was a minor when the document was said to have been signed and that another purported signatory was outside India at the time.
A civil suit seeking cancellation of the power of attorney was pending; another suit referred to by the appellant had been dismissed for non-prosecution, with no evidence that it had been restored.
The High Court declined to quash the criminal proceedings, and the Supreme Court considered an appeal from that refusal.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the refusal to quash the criminal proceedings and dismissed the appeal, holding that the pending civil suit did not warrant quashing in light of the serious allegations.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, inherent powers to quash proceedings at the initial stage are to be exercised sparingly, including where the allegations, taken at face value and in their entirety, do not prima facie disclose an offence. Disputed or controversial facts cannot form the basis for quashing. A criminal complaint is not to be quashed merely because a civil suit is pending if the allegations are not frivolous, mala fide, or vexatious. The Court relied on Arun Bhandari v. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2013) 2 SCC 801, and Kamaladevi Agarwal v. State of W.B., (2002) 1 SCC 555.

rule.if: appeal_from_refusal_to_quash and fir_alleges_forged_authority_document and fir_alleges_signer_was_a_minor and fir_alleges_another_signer_was_abroad and civil_suit_concerns_the_same_dispute

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_quash: The accused appealed after a court refused to quash the criminal proceedings.
predicates.fir_alleges_forged_authority_document: The first information report alleged that the accused procured an authority document by forging the signatures of purported signatories.
predicates.fir_alleges_signer_was_a_minor: The first information report alleged that one purported signatory was a minor when the document was said to have been signed.
predicates.fir_alleges_another_signer_was_abroad: The first information report alleged that another purported signatory was outside the country when the document was said to have been signed.
predicates.civil_suit_concerns_the_same_dispute: A civil suit concerning the property or authority document underlying the criminal allegations was pending.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a refusal to quash, the first information report alleges a forged authority document and circumstances casting doubt on the purported signatures, and a civil suit concerns the same dispute, the criminal proceedings are not quashed.
